keyVerseText: So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew word אָרוֹן (ʼârôwn) derives from the root אָרָה (ʼârâh), which means 'to gather' or 'to pluck.' This etymology suggests that the term originally conveyed the idea of a container or vessel designed to gather and hold items together. Beyond its common English gloss as 'ark' or 'chest,' the root emphasizes the function of bringing things into one place, highlighting the word's role as a repository or holder.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, אָרוֹן is predominantly used to refer to a chest or box, most notably the Ark of the Covenant, as reflected by its top translation 'the ark' occurring 100 times out of 202 total occurrences. It also appears as a money chest and, less frequently, as a coffin, such as in Genesis 50:26. This range of uses—from sacred containers holding the tablets of the law to coffins—reveals the word's consistent association with a physical space for safeguarding something valuable or significant.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, אָרוֹן signifies more than a mere container; it represents God's tangible presence and covenant with His people, especially in the Ark of the Covenant. Its root meaning of 'gathering' underscores the divine act of bringing together His promises and His people in a sacred space. This word reminds believers that God is both a protector and a unifier, holding His covenant and His people securely. Understanding אָרוֹן enriches our appreciation of how God makes Himself known and accessible, foreshadowing Christ as the ultimate fulfillment of God's presence dwelling among humanity.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 50:26 states, 'So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.' Here, the word אָרוֹן is used to describe the coffin in which Joseph was placed. This usage highlights the word's broader semantic range beyond the Ark of the Covenant, emphasizing its role as a protective container even in death. It reminds us that just as the ark safeguarded God's covenant, the coffin safeguarded Joseph's body, symbolizing care and reverence in both life and death.
